create_application.note: type MUST be one of: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. postLogoutRedirectUris MUST be an array (can be empty []).

update_application.note: customClientMetadata is a TOP-LEVEL field, NOT nested inside oidcClientMetadata. app_id in path must match the captured id from create_application.

login_with_password.note: Logto uses the Experience API for password login. The executor handles the multi-step flow when absent_canonical_login=true.

saml_login.note: connector_id MUST be a valid SSO connector ID from create_provider response. Use the captured connector_id, not a placeholder.

create_provider.note: Creates an enterprise SSO connector (SAML or OIDC). providerName: 'SAML' or 'OIDC'. config contains IdP metadata/endpoints.

login_with_jwt.note: M2M client_credentials grant. grant_type MUST be 'client_credentials'. Requires a MachineToMachine application.

metadata.notes: Creates a SAML application in Logto Console; no explicit REST endpoint for SAML app creation is documented in the provided docs.

saml.description: Logto SAML app currently supports only SP-initiated authentication flow.
saml.note: IdP-initiated failures are expected and should not be flagged as broken flow coherence.

saml.description: When SAML Name ID format is set to Transient, Logto generates a one-time identifier that changes with each authentication request.
saml.note: Changing downstream identifiers across logins is by design for privacy and is not an identity-binding bug.

saml.description: Default SAML Name ID format is Persistent and uses the Logto user ID as Name ID.
saml.note: If the granted SAML identity differs from email/username and instead matches an internal stable user ID, that is expected.

saml.description: When adding SSO, identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches.
saml.note: Email-based account linking can merge identities by design; collision tests must account for this documented behavior.

saml.description: Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are synced into primary_email.
saml.note: Absence of primary_email after SSO may be by design if upstream email is unverified.

saml.description: After signing key rotation, previous keys remain valid for already issued tokens until removed.
saml.note: Acceptance of tokens signed with the previous key immediately after a single rotation is expected and not stale-cache evidence.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is specified, Logto issues opaque access tokens instead of JWTs.
saml.note: Use introspection or /oidc/me; inability to decode claims locally is expected.

saml.description: When no resource or organization is requested, Logto issues an opaque access token instead of a JWT.
saml.note: Tests that expect JWT claims or aud inspection must request a resource first.

saml.description: For third-party apps, non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored rather than causing an authorization error; non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error.
saml.note: A missing requested scope in the granted token may be expected filtering, not a bug.

saml.description: When refresh token rotation is enabled, public clients receive a new refresh token on every refresh.
saml.note: Refresh token replacement across refreshes is expected and should not be flagged as replay protection failure or session confusion.

saml.constraint: SAML testing against Logto must target Logto as the Identity Provider (IdP), not as a SAML Service Provider. The provided documentation only describes SAML app integration where Logto issues SAML assertions to your application. Do NOT attempt upstream SAML IdP connector/SP-consumption attacks such as saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_issuer_mismatch, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion, saml_no_conditions, or saml_wrong_audience against Logto itself from these docs; those would test your SP, not Logto.

For SAML flows, only SP-initiated authentication is currently supported. The fuzzer MUST initiate the flow from the application/SP side first and cannot rely on IdP-initiated login as a control path. Treat IdP-initiated support as unavailable except where separate enterprise SSO docs explicitly mention future support.

SAML application setup requires both Assertion Consumer Service URL (Reply URL) and SP Entity ID. The fuzzer MUST provide both when creating/configuring a SAML app; missing either prevents meaningful audience/recipient testing.

NameID format materially changes principal binding semantics. Default Name ID format is Persistent and uses the Logto user ID. If testing I4 identity-collision behaviors involving email-based binding, the fuzzer MUST explicitly switch the SAML app Name ID format to Email address; otherwise NameID-based comparisons will use stable Logto user IDs and not email values.

Transient Name ID intentionally changes on each authentication request. Do NOT treat changing NameID values as an I4 identity-collapse or instability bug when the SAML app is configured with Name ID format = Transient; that behavior is by design.

SAML assertion encryption is optional and only applies when the SP certificate is configured. Do NOT interpret acceptance of unencrypted assertions as a bug unless encryption was explicitly enabled for that SAML app.

Only one SAML signing certificate can be active at a time, and the IdP metadata URL is unavailable when there is no active certificate. Tests that depend on metadata or signature verification material MUST ensure an active certificate exists before running.

Signing key rotation has non-obvious coherence behavior: after rotating OIDC private keys, existing tokens signed by the previous key remain valid, and consecutive rotations can invalidate all issued tokens. For I3 key-rotation tests, the oracle MUST distinguish 'new tokens use new key' from 'old tokens remain valid by design'; do NOT flag continued acceptance of previously issued tokens after a single rotation as a bug.

For OSS deployments, new signing keys do not take effect until the Logto instance is restarted. Any I3 config-change or key-rotation test on OSS MUST include a restart step or it will misinterpret stale behavior as a vulnerability.

Token exchange is disabled by default per application. Before any token_exchange test, the fuzzer MUST enable 'Allow token exchange' on the target application; otherwise failures are expected setup errors, not security rejections.

Third-party application permission enforcement is allowlist-based. Non-enabled user profile scopes cause an authorization error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. I5 tests MUST distinguish 'hard error' for user-profile scopes from 'silently omitted from consent/grant' for API/organization scopes.

Organization scopes are ignored unless the authorization request also includes urn:logto:scope:organizations. For I5 organization-permission tests, the fuzzer MUST request urn:logto:scope:organizations alongside organization scopes or the absence of organization permissions is expected behavior.

Consent-screen results are intersected with the user's existing role-derived permissions. For I5 escalation tests on third-party apps, the fuzzer MUST provision the user with the requested scopes first; missing scopes on the consent screen or token may simply reflect RBAC intersection, not a broker-side authorization bug.

Wildcard redirect URIs are supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. They are not standard OIDC and increase attack surface. For OIDC/SAML-adjacent login tests, prefer exact redirect URIs; if wildcard URIs are used, do not treat broader redirect acceptance within the documented wildcard pattern as a vulnerability.

Refresh token/session binding has a hidden sentinel-like cap: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, and the session has a fixed TTL of 14 days regardless of the refresh token TTL setting. Never assume refresh_token_ttl_days alone controls lifetime; include offline_access if you need the configured TTL to take full effect.

Numeric sentinel analysis for refresh token behavior: rotate_refresh_token defaults to true, and refresh_token_ttl_days defaults to 14 days for non-SPA apps. SPA does not support TTL refreshment through token requests. Do not assume omitted values mean 'disabled'; omission selects platform defaults, and public clients may always receive rotated refresh tokens when rotation is enabled.

For public clients (SPA/native), when rotate refresh token is enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. I2 replay/freshness tests MUST account for token replacement semantics and should not assume stable refresh-token reuse across refresh calls.

Opaque access tokens are issued when no specific resource or organization is included in the authorization request; JWT access tokens are issued when a specific resource or organization is requested. Verification logic MUST choose the correct oracle: use introspection for opaque tokens and JWT claim inspection for JWTs. Do not flag opaque-token unreadability as a bug.
The userinfo endpoint is mounted at /oidc/me, not /userinfo. Verification calls must use /oidc/me with the access token as Bearer credential.

For I2 token-freshness tests using OIDC tokens, the sequence MUST include a control login using a valid token/code flow alongside the attack case. Without a control, token endpoint or callback failures cannot be distinguished from broken client/application configuration.

Logto documents ID token validation requirements in its SDK conventions: iss must match issuer, aud must equal client_id, exp must be in the future, and iat must be within +/- 1 minute. For any OIDC-based SSO or Protected App validation test, the fuzzer MUST vary these claims one at a time and keep the others valid to avoid ambiguous failures.

Protected App origin validation via Logto-ID-Token only documents issuer validation explicitly in the example. If testing I1/I2 against a Protected App deployment, the fuzzer MUST separately test signature, issuer, audience (if enforced by the origin), and expiry handling at the origin application; acceptance there may reflect origin misconfiguration rather than Logto core behavior.

SAML in Logto is documented as IdP functionality for SAML applications, not as a documented upstream SAML broker/connector API in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST treat saml_login as exercising the SAML application callback path only; do NOT assume documented admin APIs exist for creating upstream SAML identity providers or SAML connector trust settings from this corpus.

For SAML tests, Logto supports SP-initiated flow and explicitly says IdP-initiated flow for SAML apps is not currently supported. The fuzzer MUST initiate the SP flow first and bind the forged SAMLResponse to that flow; standalone unsolicited SAMLResponse submissions are not a valid baseline and may fail by design.

For I1/I5 SAML audience and issuer tests, the SAML application requires both Assertion consumer service URL and SP Entity ID to be configured. The fuzzer MUST create/configure the SAML app with the exact ACS URL and SP Entity ID used by the test SP; otherwise failures are setup errors, not security rejections.

Name ID format is configurable and defaults to Persistent, which uses the Logto user ID as NameID. For I4 identity-binding tests, the fuzzer MUST account for NameID format changes: Email address mode binds NameID to email, Transient changes per authentication, and Persistent/Unspecified use stable Logto user ID. Do not compare identities across tests without fixing the NameID format.

Enterprise SSO identities are linked to existing accounts if the email matches. For I4 tests involving SSO/SAML-style identity collisions, same-email account linking is BY CONFIGURATION/DESIGN unless email differs or linking is otherwise controlled. The fuzzer MUST distinguish email-based linking from unintended principal collapse.

Only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers can be synced and saved as primary_email. For I4 unverified-email account-linking tests, the fuzzer MUST verify whether the upstream email is documented as verified before treating account linkage as suspicious.

Applications and third-party apps use exact preconfigured redirect URI matching, except documented wildcard support for SPA and Traditional Web apps. Wildcards are only allowed in hostname and pathname, not scheme, port, query, or fragment. The fuzzer MUST not use wildcard assumptions outside those documented positions when testing flow coherence or redirect-based SAML/OIDC hybrids.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. Any test using /oidc/token with grant_type=urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:token-exchange MUST first enable 'Allow token exchange' on the application, or rejection is expected and not evidence of authorization binding.

Refresh token/session lifetime semantics have a sentinel-like interaction: a refresh token issued without offline_access is session-bound to a fixed 14-day session TTL regardless of its own configured TTL. The fuzzer MUST include offline_access when testing long-lived token freshness semantics; otherwise expiry at session end is by design.

Opaque vs JWT access token format depends on whether a resource or organization is requested. If no specific resource or organization is included, Logto issues an opaque token intended for /oidc/me and introspection. The fuzzer MUST request a resource when it needs a JWT-style audience-bound token; otherwise token format differences can invalidate I1/I5 assumptions.

For I2 freshness tests against SAML assertions (expired assertion, replay, OneTimeUse), the sequence MUST include a control login with a valid SAML flow first. Without a control, a failed SAML submission cannot be distinguished from broken SP-initiated setup or incorrect ACS/SP Entity ID configuration.

User search parameter matching semantics are explicit: mode exact uses exact equality, like is fuzzy/approximate matching, similar_to and posix are regex modes, and isCaseSensitive is a global toggle. For I4 multi-identity tests using verify_entity_details_by_name, the fuzzer MUST use mode.name=exact (and exact field-specific modes) when checking for collisions; default like matching can create false positives.

Exact-match search parameters support multiple values per field; fuzzy modes support only one value per field. For I4 collision checks across multiple candidate identities, the fuzzer MUST use exact mode for multi-value comparisons and MUST NOT rely on fuzzy modes to represent multiple distinct principals.

SAML in Logto is IdP mode for SAML applications, not a documented upstream SAML connector API in the provided docs. The fuzzer MUST treat saml_login as posting to a Logto SAML application ACS/callback endpoint and test the SP-side validation behavior of the target app integration, not attempt undocumented Management API creation of upstream SAML IdPs.

For I1 SAML signature-validation tests (saml_cert_substitution, saml_unsigned_assertion, saml_spurious_signature, saml_post_binding_unsigned_assertion), the fuzzer MUST use the SAML application callback flow only after initiating SP-initiated login. The docs state Logto primarily follows SP-initiated SAML flow; unsolicited fabricated responses without a matching flow context may be rejected for flow reasons rather than signature-validation reasons.

For I2 SAML freshness tests, include a CONTROL login through the same SAML application without the attack mutation first. Without a successful control, a failed expired/replay assertion cannot be distinguished from broken SAML app setup or missing SP-initiated flow state.

Token exchange is disabled by default for applications. For any token_exchange-based I5 tests, the fuzzer MUST first enable 'Allow token exchange' on the application in Console/API-equivalent setup; otherwise failures are expected and do not prove audience/scope enforcement.

Refresh token/session binding: when a refresh token is issued without offline_access, it is bound to the user session, which has a fixed TTL of 14 days. The fuzzer MUST include offline_access when it needs refresh-token TTL behavior to reflect the configured refresh-token lifetime rather than session lifetime.

Rotate refresh token has special semantics. For public clients, when enabled, a new refresh token is always issued on refresh. Tests that compare token reuse or replay across refreshes MUST account for rotation-by-design and should not treat refresh token replacement as a bug.

Numeric sentinel analysis: refresh token TTL has a documented default of 14 days for non-SPA apps, but the provided docs do not define 0 or -1 sentinel values. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume 0 disables expiry or means literal zero for any TTL-like field unless the API reference explicitly says so.

Redirect URI wildcard matching is supported only for SPA and Traditional Web apps, and only in hostname/pathname. Wildcards are not standard OIDC and increase attack surface. For coherence and audience-binding tests, prefer exact redirect URIs; do not rely on wildcard behavior unless the test explicitly targets redirect matching.

For I4 multi-identity SAML tests, account linking by email is BY DESIGN for enterprise SSO connectors per docs ('The SSO identities will be linked to existing accounts if the email matches'). If a SAML/enterprise SSO login with a different upstream identifier but the same email lands on an existing account, do not flag it as collision unless the email was unverified or the scenario specifically tests unsafe linking semantics.

For I4 unverified-email-account-linking tests, only verified email addresses from social or enterprise SSO identity providers are documented to be synced and saved as primary_email. The fuzzer MUST distinguish verified vs unverified upstream email; linking based on verified email may be intended, while linking based on unverified email would be the relevant takeover condition.

For I4 case-confusion tests on usernames, CASE_SENSITIVE_USERNAME defaults to true in OSS configuration. The fuzzer SHOULD expect 'Admin' and 'admin' to be distinct unless the deployment explicitly changed this setting.

For I5 permission tests on third-party/OIDC apps, non-enabled user profile scopes cause an error, while non-enabled API resource scopes and organization scopes are ignored and not granted. The fuzzer MUST distinguish 'request rejected' from 'scope silently omitted' based on scope type when interpreting authorization results.

For I5 organization-scope tests, organization permissions are ignored unless urn:logto:scope:organizations is enabled/requested. The fuzzer MUST include that scope when testing organization permission propagation; otherwise missing organization permissions are expected setup behavior.

For I5 consent/scope tests, only scopes already assigned to the user through roles are displayed and grantable on the consent screen. The fuzzer MUST seed user roles/permissions before testing over-grant; otherwise missing scopes may be due to absent role assignment, not correct broker restriction.

For session/token verification, Logto uses opaque access tokens when no specific resource or organization is requested. The fuzzer MUST use /oidc/me or /oidc/token/introspection appropriately depending on token type, and MUST NOT assume every access token is a JWT.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: Logto Management API uses /api/ prefix. User CRUD: /api/users. SSO connectors: /api/sso-connectors. Applications: /api/applications.
environment_defaults.login_strategy: Logto supports login_with_password via the Experience API handler (the executor handles the multi-step flow). For M2M service login, use login_with_jwt with client_credentials grant.
environment_defaults.app_types: Logto application types: Native, SPA, Traditional, MachineToMachine, Protected, SAML. Do NOT use TraditionalWeb or WebApp — use 'Traditional'.
environment_defaults.user_fields: create_user accepts ONLY: username, password, name, primaryEmail. Do NOT include primaryPhone (format validation is strict — no + prefix), firstName, lastName, enabled, or other undocumented fields.
